mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate suggests a weakening labor market, which could lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 exhibits positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods following a UNRATE increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, which may boost corporate revenues and lead to positive S&P 500 returns in the short term.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth is followed by negative S&P 500 returns in more than 60% of the 5-day windows, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 may signal supply chain issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO falls below 95 but S&P 500 returns remain positive in more than 40% of the 60-day periods, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling employment (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of the 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) coupled with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) may lead to stagflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth slows and CPIAUCSL rises but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the 60-day periods, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) may lead to higher borrowing costs and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases above 2% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the 20-day periods, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) combined with increased consumer spending (RSAFS) may indicate an imbalanced economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines and RSAFS increases but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 35% of the 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.
